conflicts.kind: motor overcurrent path: no hardware actuation path
conflicts.description: V288 and V159 require the ESC pack switch to open within the 500 ms stop deadline after a motor overcurrent or over-temperature detection. The detection chain reaches the main coprocessor in about 18 ms (INA228 ALERT within 17.0 ms, 74VHC21FT 8.5 ns, 1 ms pass; the MCP9808 at the onboard shunt 60 to 500 ms by resolution) and the coprocessor disarms its outputs. The pack switch drivers (TPSI3052DWZR) take the latch output alone: no coprocessor input exists (V53, V160), the Not defeatable rule allows none, and docs/Safety.md states that no hardware covers a healthy panel with a misbehaving coprocessor. The switch opens only when the panel's heartbeat stops (enable falls 155 to 185 ms later, switch open within 5 ms), and no coprocessor action stops it. A path through the panel (fault bit read at a 50 ms poll, STOP, heartbeat) adds up to 17 + 20 + 50 + 185 + 5 = 277 ms plus a panel reaction time that no page defines.
conflicts.evidence: FU-2A/012-P2-R3.json found V53; FU-2I/002-P2-R8.json found V159, V160 and reports 'Motor overcurrent path for P5', 'Over-temperature trip timing for P5'; docs/Safety.md 'Required external circuit: the monostable' (third row); Research.md V1, V288; IOBoard.md Link and safety (Not defeatable)

conflicts.kind: rail conflict: pack path drop allowance and pack protection window
conflicts.description: V294 allows 0.2 V from the cells to the converters at 52.1 A (3.8 mOhm for the protector MOSFETs, ideal-diode MOSFETs, 1 mOhm shunt, XT60 and wiring). The BQ25723RSNR's battery sense resistor RSR (5 mOhm, in the pack-to-load path) alone drops 0.261 V and 13.6 W at 52.1 A, 0.313 V with the BQ40Z80's 1 mOhm shunt, before the BATFET and the MOSFETs. With 6 mOhm in the path and the converter loads at the verified efficiencies (305.0 W), the pack current at the 6.0 V sizing corner is 53.8 A (54.9 A at 8 mOhm, 56.1 A at 10 mOhm), above the BQ40Z80's untrimmed lower overcurrent edge of 52.21 A and above the post-trim edge of 55.25 A beyond 8.6 mOhm. At the 6.6 V floor of V294 the current is 47.3 to 50.1 A and inside both windows, and the converters' inductor clamps keep the draw at 31 to 35 A (7 to 8 A each, no maximum stated). At the 100.68 A upper short-circuit edge the RSR drops 0.503 V, over the BQ25723's 0.5 V SRP-SRN absolute maximum for up to 915 microseconds. Whether one P-channel BATFET carries 52.1 A is not known. The cell's 90 A continuous rating and the 60 A path rating hold.
conflicts.evidence: FU-2H/003-P2-R7.json reports 'charger battery path loss and drop', 'protector overcurrent windows', 'protector short-circuit windows', 'stage 2 MOSFETs: charger BATFET and switches'; FU-2F/012-adjudicator-R7-4.json (RSR figures reproduce); FU-2I/003-P2-R5.json 'pack path drop allowance'; BQ25723 https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq25723.pdf (read 2026-10-03T08:37:22Z): SRP-SRN -0.5 to 0.5 V, RSNS_RSR 5 mOhm or 10 mOhm; Research.md V294, V309; P5 arithmetic scratch/FU-2P56/P5/calc.py (2026-10-03T08:35Z)

conflicts.description: The external CAN transceiver TCAN1472VDRQ1 is in standby with STB high and in normal mode with STB low (STB has an integrated pull-up), while the enable node is high when enabled. The standby input therefore needs an inverter with I_off from the enable node, as FU-2A noted. No function in selection.json names it, and SN74LVC1G04DBVR is booked for the 244 output enables only (R3 1 to 2, R4 1 to 2 placements, summed 4; 5 with this inverter). The external CAN port would stay in normal mode, or with an undriven STB in standby, rather than follow the enable node.

conflicts.kind: function without a part on the ESC pack node
conflicts.description: The ADBMS1818's V+ must be at or above C18 - 0.3 V and C18 may not exceed V+ + 5.5 V, with unused inputs tied to the top cell. The always-on supply LTM8068EY#PBF gives a fixed 18 V on VOUT1 (17.7 V after an OR drop): it misses TME for packs above 18.0 V (5 cells at 4.2 V) and exceeds the absolute limit above 23.2 V (6 cells), so V+ for 1 to 16 cells up to 67.2 V needs an OR element from each tap that can be the pack top (blocks up to 67.2 V, 85 V rating, drop at most 0.3 V at 1.4 mA). FU-2D reported that no function names it. It sits on the ESC pack node and has no part in selection.json, so the node's check against the clamp level cannot include it.
conflicts.evidence: FU-2D/003-P2-R9.json reports 'V+ feed from the highest tap', 'V+ OR element ratings'; ADBMS1818 Rev. B Tables 3 and 11 as read in FU-2D (2026-10-02T06:21:10Z); Research.md V189, V193, V289, F15; selection.json R9

conflicts.kind: rail conflict: USB-C-powered logic supply exceeds the source current
conflicts.description: V91 (found, FU-2I) has the shared USB-C connector power the board through the BQ25723RSNR VSYS (6.6 V) when neither the DC input nor the pack is present, 'within the source's advertised current'. P5 returned no budget for this rail. Loads with the servo converters off, at P5's own efficiencies: 3.3 V rail 1,562 mA (1,662 mA with the 100 mA TCND5000 bound) = 5.4 to 5.8 W at VSYS; 5 V rail 2.08 A peak (display 2.0 A + TCAN1472 80 mA) = 10.8 W, 1.58 A continuous = 8.2 W; load-cell regulator 0.26 W: 16.5 to 16.9 W peak, 13.9 to 14.3 W continuous (encoder 1.3 W and LTM8068 not counted). Available: 3 A x 5 V = 15 W (F8) x 94.7 % (BQ25723 VBUS to VSYS, V139) = 14.2 W. Peak exceeds it by 2.3 to 2.7 W; continuous is at it; a 500 mA default source (2.5 W) cannot carry the 3.3 V rail alone. FU-2I states only 'exceeds a 500 mA default source'. The LM61460's efficiency is not read.

conflicts.description: The Research.md R5 row says R5 states it as a conflict if the display does not isolate its VBUS. FU-2I and FU-2F returned it: the display's Type_C2 VBUS joins its 5V net with only a TVS to ground (V80, found: 'No'), so link power from the TPS259474ARPWR reaches the VBUS pin of the display's native USB-C socket and back-feeds a host or charger plugged there. The IO board side blocks reverse current (V266), which does not stop the forward feed. Connecting both at once is not specified as safe. P5 returned no entry for it.

conflicts.kind: PIO bind order: programming mode refused
conflicts.description: Combination 'every mix ... 68 of 81' says a port in a programming mode is allocated as 2 state machines and at most 16 words. pico-sdk 2.3.0 pio.c:454-508 does not reserve a port's freed space: a PIO UART bound with the same call as out_dshot.c (tx 4 words, rx 9 words, one pin) is placed where it finds a free state machine, and a block that holds PPM first stays at GPIO base 0 and cannot take pins 32 and up. Switching one port into a programming mode after the stated bind order is refused in 12 of the (mix, port) cases of the 68 allowed mixes: BBBN port 4 (N to programming), BBNB port 3, BNBB port 2, NBBB port 1, BBPP ports 3 and 4, BPPB ports 2 and 3, PBPB ports 1 and 3, PPBB ports 1 and 2 (B bidirectional, P plain, N no PIO output). A port that was bidirectional always rebinds. Programming binds that happen before the 4 ports and the socket (combination 'all four in programming mode') fit: 11 state machines, 69 words.

The clause 'a port in a programming mode is allocated as 2 state machines and at most 16 words' is not guaranteed by the allocator: the SDK reserves nothing per port. assumptions.value: 2 PIO state machines on the measurement coprocessor, both in PIO1: 1 receive and 1 transmit, 13 instruction words (UART receive 9 + transmit 4, sized from the pico-examples UART programs, which are not in the tree); one receiver input on GPIO 23 (V68); the receive program takes the S.BUS 8E2 100 kbaud frame with the pad's input inversion and the other buses (iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2, JETI EX Bus) as UART; the transmit state machine drives GPIO 23 through SN74LVC1T45DBVR, whose direction pin takes 1 more GPIO (counted in GPIO: measurement). A hardware UART is available for the receive-only buses: UART1 is free on this chip and GPIO 23 has UART1_RX (funcsel 0x0b), but UART1_TX would need GPIO 20, 22, 24 or 26, which the encoder, the chip select and the TCA9548A reset hold, so the transmit direction needs PIO.
assumptions.why: No receiver PIO program is written (docs/Receivers.md); V71 (owner, 2026-09-28) says the bench transmits on a receiver input for JETI EX Bus and SRXL2; the map puts the receiver on PIO1; the count must be stated and the count for transmit is the smallest that meets V71.
assumptions.source: hardware/docs/pinmap.json measurement GPIO 23; Research.md V68, V71; docs/Receivers.md:10-16 and shared/sbus/include/sbus.h:4-17 in the checkout; ~/toolchains/pico-sdk io_bank0.h GPIO23 funcsel table; hardware/docs/Pins.md Not known (receive-only)
assumptions.reason: The tree states no receiver PIO program (docs/Receivers.md; Research.md V68, V71). 2 state machines and 13 words match pico-examples uart_rx (9 words) and uart_tx (4 words), counted from the raw files read 2026-10-03T09:01:33Z; the 9-bit frame for S.BUS 8E2 parity keeps the word count. GPIO 23 UART1_RX at funcsel 0x0b confirmed in io_bank0.h, UART1_TX would need GPIO 20, 22, 24 or 26, which the map holds, so the transmit direction needs PIO. Reasonable and sourced.

assumptions.value: 0 state machines beyond the 8 booked for bidirectional DShot on the 4 multiprotocol ports: a port runs one protocol at a time, so the programmer's one-wire bootloader (BLHeli_S and AM32, 19,200 baud, half duplex), ESCape32 CLI and Hitec D-series run as PIO UART programs (transmit 4 + receive 9 words, assumed) on the 2 state machines and within the 16 words of that port's DShot allocation; DShot's teardown() releases the state machines and words before the new program loads (out_dshot.c:113-127). VESC's 115,200 baud runs on UART1 (GPIO 4, 5, V67), not on a state machine. If a mode needs a third state machine on one port, the main chip has 1 spare (11 of 12 booked), enough for one port at a time.
assumptions.why: No programmer protocol has run on a wire (STATUS.md, shared/ui/programmer_screen.c:237-248), the levels, form and baud of Hitec D-series and the ESCape32 baud are not stated (V59 to V62, for research), and each bound output loads its own copy of its program, so a count has to be assumed.
assumptions.source: firmware/iomcu/src/out_dshot.c:113-127 and dshot.pio in the checkout; hardware/docs/IOBoard.md Programming on the multiprotocol ports; Research.md V59 to V62, V67; hardware/docs/Pins.md Owner decisions
assumptions.reason: The tree states no programmer program or count. 2 state machines and 13 words are sized from pico-examples uart_tx 4 and uart_rx 9 (read 2026-10-03T09:01:33Z); all four ports in programming mode bind with 11 of 12 state machines and 69 words in my model (2026-10-03T09:07:25Z). The count holds. The clause 'within the 16 words of that port's DShot allocation' holds only for a port that was bidirectional; from plain or unbound ports the SDK refuses 12 cases (see combination 2 and the added item).

assumptions.value: 5 ms (a 200 Hz current sensor): the measurement coprocessor reads each INA3221 and checks the 3.0 A ceiling at every sample; the INA3221 refreshes its 3 channels in 3.63 ms at most, so each channel gives a fresh value at every 5 ms sample.
assumptions.why: The tree does not state the period of the coprocessor's port-current sample; docs/Servo.md:35 says 'checked at every sample' and the host test models the sensor at 5 ms. Round 1's P5 assumed 20 ms, the BENCH sampling period, which its critic rejected: that period belongs to the motor monitor's BENCH reading.
assumptions.source: test/host/test_servo_limit.c:19 ('#define SAMPLE_MS 5u /* a 200 Hz current sensor */') and docs/Servo.md:35 in checkout-f0306687a475; FU-2I/002-P2-R8.json found V173 (read 2026-10-03T00:15:40Z); round1/T5/004-P5-critic.json added item on the sample period
assumptions.reason: The tree states no sample period for the coprocessor: docs/Servo.md:35 says 'checked at every sample'; test/host/test_servo_limit.c:19 models 'SAMPLE_MS 5u, a 200 Hz current sensor'. 5 ms is sourced and reasonable: the INA3221 refreshes 3 channels in at most 3.63 ms and a bus A sweep reads in 1.38 ms.

Both the FU-2A selection and the R11 phase-wire clip's 120 V input figure (V214) rest on this clamp. No later run covers R3.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V75 (R4, series resistance and clamps): faults the buffer must survive on a connector signal line
gaps.description: The found value is refuted and not re-run. FU-A3/010-P4-datasheet-R4.json (found V75, verdict refuted, read_at 2026-09-29T05:40:35Z and 05:36:57Z): V75's 275 Ohm and 142 Ohm lower bounds cover only the short to ground; for the 8.7 V short to the port supply pin the pad-driven line carries (8.7 - 0.5) V / 275 Ohm = 29.8 mA into the pad against the 12 mA highest drive setting (RP2350 Table 1436), and 245 mW in the resistor, not 95 mW. The series resistance and clamp function is stage 2 (resistors, connector protection), but the fault current it must hold is not established. R4 was not run in round 2; the harness lists 'R4 figure found V75 not confirmed in FU-A3' as accepted open.

item.kind: motor overcurrent path: no hardware actuation path
item.description: V288 and V159 require the ESC pack switch to open within the 500 ms stop deadline after a motor overcurrent or over-temperature detection. The detection chain reaches the main coprocessor in about 18 ms (INA228 ALERT within 17.0 ms, 74VHC21FT 8.5 ns, 1 ms pass; the MCP9808 at the onboard shunt 60 to 500 ms by resolution) and the coprocessor disarms its outputs. The pack switch drivers (TPSI3052DWZR) take the latch output alone: no coprocessor input exists (V53, V160), the Not defeatable rule allows none, and docs/Safety.md states that no hardware covers a healthy panel with a misbehaving coprocessor. The switch opens only when the panel's heartbeat stops (enable falls 155 to 185 ms later, switch open within 5 ms), and no coprocessor action stops it. A path through the panel (fault bit read at a 50 ms poll, STOP, heartbeat) adds up to 17 + 20 + 50 + 185 + 5 = 277 ms plus a panel reaction time that no page defines.
item.evidence: FU-2A/012-P2-R3.json found V53; FU-2I/002-P2-R8.json found V159, V160 and reports 'Motor overcurrent path for P5', 'Over-temperature trip timing for P5'; docs/Safety.md 'Required external circuit: the monostable' (third row); Research.md V1, V288; IOBoard.md Link and safety (Not defeatable)

item.kind: PIO bind order: programming mode refused
item.description: Combination 'every mix ... 68 of 81' says a port in a programming mode is allocated as 2 state machines and at most 16 words. pico-sdk 2.3.0 pio.c:454-508 does not reserve a port's freed space: a PIO UART bound with the same call as out_dshot.c (tx 4 words, rx 9 words, one pin) is placed where it finds a free state machine, and a block that holds PPM first stays at GPIO base 0 and cannot take pins 32 and up. Switching one port into a programming mode after the stated bind order is refused in 12 of the (mix, port) cases of the 68 allowed mixes: BBBN port 4 (N to programming), BBNB port 3, BNBB port 2, NBBB port 1, BBPP ports 3 and 4, BPPB ports 2 and 3, PBPB ports 1 and 3, PPBB ports 1 and 2 (B bidirectional, P plain, N no PIO output). A port that was bidirectional always rebinds. Programming binds that happen before the 4 ports and the socket (combination 'all four in programming mode') fit: 11 state machines, 69 words.

Over-temperature: two consecutive conversions above each limit; the MCP9808 at the onboard shunt takes 60, 130, 260 or 500 ms at 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625 degC (the default 0.0625 degC leaves no room in 500 ms, so firmware writes 0.25 degC: 195 ms with the crossing inside a conversion). To the ESC pack switch: no path. The TPSI3052DWZR switch drivers take the latch output alone, and the coprocessor cannot remove or add to the enable (V53, V160, Not defeatable); docs/Safety.md states that no hardware covers a healthy panel with a misbehaving coprocessor. V288 and V159 require the switch to open within the 500 ms stop deadline, and nothing in the design carries that: the switch opens only when the panel's heartbeat stops (enable falls 155 to 185 ms later, switch within 5 ms), which no coprocessor action causes. If a panel reaction on the fault bit were defined, 17 + 20 + 50 + 185 + 5 = 277 ms plus the panel's reaction would have to stay under 223 ms; none is defined. Not within.

conflicts.kind: motor overcurrent path: no hardware actuation path
conflicts.description: V288 and V159 require the ESC pack switch to open within the 500 ms stop deadline after a motor overcurrent or over-temperature detection. The detection chain reaches the main coprocessor in about 18 ms (INA228 ALERT within 17.0 ms, 74VHC21FT 8.5 ns, 1 ms pass; the MCP9808 at the onboard shunt 60 to 500 ms by resolution) and the coprocessor disarms its outputs. The pack switch drivers (TPSI3052DWZR) take the latch output alone: no coprocessor input exists (V53, V160), the Not defeatable rule allows none, and docs/Safety.md states that no hardware covers a healthy panel with a misbehaving coprocessor. The switch opens only when the panel's heartbeat stops (enable falls 155 to 185 ms later, switch open within 5 ms), and no coprocessor action stops it. A path through the panel (fault bit read at a 50 ms poll, STOP, heartbeat) adds up to 17 + 20 + 50 + 185 + 5 = 277 ms plus a panel reaction time that no page defines.

conflicts.kind: rail conflict: pack path drop allowance and pack protection window
conflicts.description: V294 allows 0.2 V from the cells to the converters at 52.1 A (3.8 mOhm for the protector MOSFETs, ideal-diode MOSFETs, 1 mOhm shunt, XT60 and wiring). The BQ25723RSNR's battery sense resistor RSR (5 mOhm, in the pack-to-load path) alone drops 0.261 V and 13.6 W at 52.1 A, 0.313 V with the BQ40Z80's 1 mOhm shunt, before the BATFET and the MOSFETs. With 6 mOhm in the path and the converter loads at the verified efficiencies (305.0 W), the pack current at the 6.0 V sizing corner is 53.8 A (54.9 A at 8 mOhm, 56.1 A at 10 mOhm), above the BQ40Z80's untrimmed lower overcurrent edge of 52.21 A and above the post-trim edge of 55.25 A beyond 8.6 mOhm. At the 6.6 V floor of V294 the current is 47.3 to 50.1 A and inside both windows, and the converters' inductor clamps keep the draw at 31 to 35 A (7 to 8 A each, no maximum stated). At the 100.68 A upper short-circuit edge the RSR drops 0.503 V, over the BQ25723's 0.5 V SRP-SRN absolute maximum for up to 915 microseconds. Whether one P-channel BATFET carries 52.1 A is not known. The cell's 90 A continuous rating and the 60 A path rating hold.

conflicts.description: The ADBMS1818's V+ must be at or above C18 - 0.3 V and C18 may not exceed V+ + 5.5 V, with unused inputs tied to the top cell. With Q8 decided as the FRAM (owner, 2026-09-29) no erase or program runs in operation, so the 400 ms stall applies to firmware updates only; the MCP2518FD holds 32 frames and the panel sends at most 9 in a 400 ms stall (V16, FU-2A). R1's watchdog finding stands: while the store was in flash no timeout met both the 500 ms stop deadline (V1) and the 900 ms longest stall (V2); with the store in the FRAM a window opens once the console write is capped (firmware).

budgets.value: Devices: 3 MCP23017, FRAM, BQ25723, BQ40Z80, FUSB303B, TPS55288. Clock: 400 kHz default (V120); the BQ40Z80 states SMBus 10 to 100 kHz (SMBus XL 40 to 400 kHz, timeout 5 to 20 ms; XL not read as a data-flash setting), so the controller runs at 100 kHz while it is addressed or XL is enabled. No device converts on this bus; the FRAM has no write wait. Per transaction: MCP23017 write 0.073 ms at 400 kHz (0.29 ms at 100 kHz); two-byte read 0.12 ms (0.48 ms); BQ40Z80 word read about 0.57 ms at 100 kHz. A 396-byte output-binding record to the FRAM is 3,591 SCL cycles: 8.98 ms at 400 kHz, 35.9 ms at 100 kHz (FU-C1); the EEPROM alternative is 7 page writes of 603 cycles plus 5 ms tW each: 10.6 ms of bus time, 45.6 ms per save. A port enable queued behind a save waits at most 9 ms (36 ms at 100 kHz), against the 80 ms and 100 ms windows. Port switches open on the expander reset (GPIO 14) within microseconds, not over I2C (V127: 5 ms). Poll load: expander read-back every 10 ms is 3.6 % of the bus at 400 kHz. Within.
budgets.source: BQ40Z80 https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq40z80.pdf (SLUSBV4D, fSMB 10-100 kHz, fSMBXL 40-400 kHz, tTIMEOUT), FU-C1/005-P2-R12.json reports 'Q8 store candidate: MB85RC256VPNF-G-AMERE2' and 'Q8 store candidate: M24256E-FMN6TP'; FU-2I/004-P2-R6.json 'Port switches through an RP2354B watchdog reset'; Research.md V120, V127; transaction bit counts i2c_calc.py

budgets.item: I2C bus timing: Qwiic and infrared bus
budgets.value: PIO I2C, TCA9548APWR, MLX90614ESF-BCC-000-TU (SMBus 10 to 100 kHz, 0x5A) and two Qwiic ports (V243 applied 400 kHz; 226 mA a port, 1 m). The MLX90614 sets the clock to 100 kHz while it is addressed; the datasheet's refresh time is 36 to 93 ms single zone, by FIR setting (128 to 1024), and it asks that SCL and SDA stay quiet for longer than the refresh time before a reading because continuous SMBus traffic induces an error on the TO39 package. A reading is 0.57 ms at 100 kHz, a mux channel select 0.20 ms. The temperature need is a reading every 2 s (V242, V236). The clock is set per transaction: 100 kHz for the MLX90614, up to 400 kHz for a Qwiic device behind the mux; the owner's 400 kHz is not met on the shared segment. A device hot-plugged on a Qwiic port may fail one transfer and is retried (V253); the TCA9548A reset on GPIO 26 clears a held channel. Within.

budgets.value: Detection to the main coprocessor: INA228 compares the averaged result (SLOWALERT 1, AVG 4, 1052 us shunt and bus): one result every 8.42 ms (8.50 ms at -1 % oscillator), ALERT within 2 results, 17.0 ms of the crossing; SOVL 30.00 mV = 150 A on 200 uOhm and 300 A on 100 uOhm (148.5 A and 285.7 A at the shunts' upper tolerance); through 1 gate of the 74VHC21FT (8.5 ns) to a main interrupt; disarm on the next 1 ms pass: about 18 ms in all, inside the 20 ms of IOBoard.md. Over-temperature: two consecutive conversions above each limit; the MCP9808 at the onboard shunt takes 60, 130, 260 or 500 ms at 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625 degC (the default 0.0625 degC leaves no room in 500 ms, so firmware writes 0.25 degC: 195 ms with the crossing inside a conversion). To the ESC pack switch: no path. The TPSI3052DWZR switch drivers take the latch output alone, and the coprocessor cannot remove or add to the enable (V53, V160, Not defeatable); docs/Safety.md states that no hardware covers a healthy panel with a misbehaving coprocessor. V288 and V159 require the switch to open within the 500 ms stop deadline, and nothing in the design carries that: the switch opens only when the panel's heartbeat stops (enable falls 155 to 185 ms later, switch within 5 ms), which no coprocessor action causes. If a panel reaction on the fault bit were defined, 17 + 20 + 50 + 185 + 5 = 277 ms plus the panel's reaction would have to stay under 223 ms; none is defined. Not within.

assumptions.value: 2 PIO state machines on the measurement coprocessor, both in PIO1: 1 receive and 1 transmit, 13 instruction words (UART receive 9 + transmit 4, sized from the pico-examples UART programs, which are not in the tree); one receiver input on GPIO 23 (V68); the receive program takes the S.BUS 8E2 100 kbaud frame with the pad's input inversion and the other buses (iBUS, SUMD, CRSF, SRXL2, JETI EX Bus) as UART; the transmit state machine drives GPIO 23 through SN74LVC1T45DBVR, whose direction pin takes 1 more GPIO (counted in GPIO: measurement). A hardware UART is available for the receive-only buses: UART1 is free on this chip and GPIO 23 has UART1_RX (funcsel 0x0b), but UART1_TX would need GPIO 20, 22, 24 or 26, which the encoder, the chip select and the TCA9548A reset hold, so the transmit direction needs PIO.
assumptions.why: No receiver PIO program is written (docs/Receivers.md); V71 (owner, 2026-09-28) says the bench transmits on a receiver input for JETI EX Bus and SRXL2; the map puts the receiver on PIO1; the count must be stated and the count for transmit is the smallest that meets V71.

added.description: The Research.md R5 row says R5 states it as a conflict if the display does not isolate its VBUS. FU-2I and FU-2F returned it: the display's Type_C2 VBUS joins its 5V net with only a TVS to ground (V80, found: 'No'), so link power from the TPS259474ARPWR reaches the VBUS pin of the display's native USB-C socket and back-feeds a host or charger plugged there. The IO board side blocks reverse current (V266), which does not stop the forward feed. Connecting both at once is not specified as safe. P5 returned no entry for it.

added.kind: PIO bind order: programming mode refused
added.description: Combination 'every mix ... 68 of 81' says a port in a programming mode is allocated as 2 state machines and at most 16 words. pico-sdk 2.3.0 pio.c:454-508 does not reserve a port's freed space: a PIO UART bound with the same call as out_dshot.c (tx 4 words, rx 9 words, one pin) is placed where it finds a free state machine, and a block that holds PPM first stays at GPIO base 0 and cannot take pins 32 and up. Switching one port into a programming mode after the stated bind order is refused in 12 of the (mix, port) cases of the 68 allowed mixes: BBBN port 4 (N to programming), BBNB port 3, BNBB port 2, NBBB port 1, BBPP ports 3 and 4, BPPB ports 2 and 3, PBPB ports 1 and 3, PPBB ports 1 and 2 (B bidirectional, P plain, N no PIO output). A port that was bidirectional always rebinds. Programming binds that happen before the 4 ports and the socket (combination 'all four in programming mode') fit: 11 state machines, 69 words.
added.evidence: model scratch/FU-2P56/P5-critic/sim.py and dyn.py run 2026-10-03T09:07:25Z over pico-sdk 2.3.0 pio.c:48-120, :454-508 and firmware/iomcu/src/out_dshot.c:73-92, :155-207; program lengths from firmware/iomcu/src/dshot.pio and ppm.pio; uart_rx 9 and uart_tx 4 words from pico-examples master (raw GitHub, read 2026-10-03T09:01:33Z)

combination_verdicts.reason: Independent model of pico-sdk 2.3.0 pio_claim_free_sm_and_add_program_for_gpio_range (pio.c:454-508, pass 0 lowest free state machine from PIO2 down, pass 1 whole empty block and base 16) and out_dshot.c claim_receiver, run 2026-10-03T09:07:25Z: ports 1 to 4 bidirectional, then socket (tx 4 + rx 9 words), then PPM on GPIO 16 binds; 11 of 12 state machines, 81 of 96 words (PIO0 17, PIO1 32, PIO2 32), all blocks at base 16. Matches P5. DMA 2 (only out_ppm.c claims DMA, grep of firmware/iomcu/src); socket program sizes are assumptions (pico-examples uart_rx 9, uart_tx 4, read 2026-10-03T09:01:33Z).
Same model: 4 plain DShot ports, socket, PPM: 7 state machines, 33 words (PIO0 0, PIO1 17, PIO2 16), blocks at base 16 or empty. Matches P5.

The count reproduces: my model over all 81 mixes of B/P/N on ports 1 to 4 in the stated order fails exactly the 13 mixes P5 lists, so 68 bind, at most 11 state machines and 81 words. IOBoard.md states in two places that no research category or question covers test access. Test points are not named in the stage 2 types of Research.md Round 2 (connectors is the nearest). Each probe lead's series resistor is 'a few hundred ohms' with no value (testbench/WIRING.md:23). They need either a stage 2 marking or a part type.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V36 (R3, monostable): drift of the timing constant k over 3.3 V +/-3 % and 0 to 50 degC
gaps.description: Found only in part. FU-2A/012-P2-R3.json (found V36, read_at 2026-10-01T21:44:26Z, 74HC423 datasheet Fig. 7 at 600 dpi): the supply term, K 0.4810 at 3.201 V, 0.4780 at 3.3 V, 0.4750 at 3.399 V, +0.63 % / -0.63 %. 'The datasheet neither graphs nor limits K against temperature, so the temperature term is not read.' The window budget (155 to 185 ms across 0 to 50 degC, V7, V38) still rests on the assumed +/-3 % of pull request #167 for that term. The FU-A2 reading (2026-09-29) also finds no part in stock that states a K limit against temperature.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V60 (R4, multiprotocol port path): Hitec D-series high level the servo drives and its input-high threshold; IOBoard.md:295
gaps.description: The servo's input-high threshold is not found. FU-A3/002-P2-R4.json (found V60, read 2026-09-29T04:38:24Z and 04:41:01Z): the programmer drives about 2 V, the servo's input-high threshold 'is not stated', and the source is a reverse-engineered library (HitecDServoInternal.h, README.md at raw.githubusercontent.com/timmaxw/HitecDServo) that states it is not endorsed by Hitec; no Hitec publication was found. The levels and baud of the protocol are 'not stated in the tree' (IOBoard.md:295). R4 was not run in round 2, so no later reading exists.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V69 (R4, receiver inputs): highest voltage a receiver drives on its signal wire; IOBoard.md:296
gaps.description: Found for SRXL2 (3.3 V logic) and CRSF (3.0 to 3.3 V) only. FU-A3/002-P2-R4.json (found V69, read 2026-09-29T04:38:22Z to 04:38:23Z and 04:41:05Z): JETI EX Bus states only a logic one of at least 3.0 V and a zero of at most 1.5 V with no maximum, SUMD (Rev 01) states no level, and for S.BUS and iBUS 'no maker specification read, level not read'. Four of the six receiver buses therefore have no stated maximum. The receiver buffer SN74LVC1T45DBVR is selected on that basis. No round 2 run covers R4.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V75 (R4, series resistance and clamps): faults the buffer must survive on a connector signal line
gaps.description: The found value is refuted and not re-run. FU-A3/010-P4-datasheet-R4.json (found V75, verdict refuted, read_at 2026-09-29T05:40:35Z and 05:36:57Z): V75's 275 Ohm and 142 Ohm lower bounds cover only the short to ground; for the 8.7 V short to the port supply pin the pad-driven line carries (8.7 - 0.5) V / 275 Ohm = 29.8 mA into the pad against the 12 mA highest drive setting (RP2350 Table 1436), and 245 mW in the resistor, not 95 mW. The series resistance and clamp function is stage 2 (resistors, connector protection), but the fault current it must hold is not established. R4 was not run in round 2; the harness lists 'R4 figure found V75 not confirmed in FU-A3' as accepted open.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V96 (R5, pack disconnect): how long a cell must stay at or below the floor before the pack disconnects; IOBoard.md:360-363
gaps.description: Not found. FU-2I/003-P2-R5.json (found V96, read_at 2026-10-03T00:22:23Z, 2026-10-02T20:33:21Z): 'No source sets a lower bound'; the maker's 3.3 V rule (SLS_Sicherheitshinweise_DE_A4.pdf section 4, read 2026-10-03T00:22:23Z) gives only an upper bound, and the fall rate depends on the pack's internal resistance, not measured (V285). The value taken, BQ40Z80 CUV:Delay 0 s (1 s steps, average trigger delay up to 1.5 s, SLUUBT5C), is P2's choice. FU-2I/021-P4-datasheet-R5.json refuted two statements of the figure (read 2026-10-03T01:28:04Z and 01:35:37Z) and adjudicator 022 upheld point 2. Listed in the owner's accepted open items of 2026-10-03.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V129 (R6, Port voltage ceiling): time within which a port must be cut off once its supply pin exceeds its ceiling, in microseconds
gaps.description: Not found. FU-2I/004-P2-R6.json (found V129, read_at 2026-10-03T00:30:20Z): 'Not found: no source read gives a time a servo survives above its rating or a cut-off time'; the Savox SH-0255MG+ and SB-2290SG pages give operating ranges and blocking currents only (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200). No P4 verifier re-read it (round2/FU-2I has no 'found V129' figure). The selected TPS3701DDCR has a response time, but the requirement it is held against is unknown. Listed in the owner's accepted open items of 2026-10-03 (R6 found V129 not found).

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V173 and V287 (R8, Port current monitor): longest time from a port exceeding 3.0 A to the abort, and the critical line's blanking time; IOBoard.md:113 and :389
gaps.description: The blanking time is not read, so V173 has no single figure. FU-2I/002-P2-R8.json (found V287 and V173, read_at 2026-10-03T00:15:40Z): the first INA3221 conversion wholly above 3.0 A completes within 3.63 + 1.21 = 4.84 ms (three channels, shunt only, CT 100, SBOS576C 6.5 and 7.4.2.1), the 74VHC21FT cascade adds 20.5 ns max, 'Blanking time: not read'. Adjudicator FU-2H/016-adjudicator-R8-3.json (2026-10-02T21:29:51Z) upheld the refutation of the blanking part: SBOS576C does not state when the Critical pin releases with three channels enabled. The owner's V323 (2026-10-03) keeps INA3221AIRGVR and has the pin's hold measured on the bench before the order, so the figure stays unknown until then. The blanking time is also a firmware choice the tree does not state (IOBoard.md:113).

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V186 (R9, Cell monitor): largest time between the first and last cell sample of one reading; IOBoard.md:475
gaps.description: Not found. FU-2D/003-P2-R9.json (found V186, read_at 2026-10-02T06:35Z): 'No source in the tree bounds how fast a cell's voltage moves under load, so no skew limit in us follows'; the only rate limit, SET_OUT_RAMP 5 to 300 %/s, applies upward (shared/outputs/outputs.c:351-356). No P4 verifier re-read it. Listed in the owner's accepted open items (R9 found V186 not found in either round).

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V187 (R9, Cell monitor): largest time between a cell voltage sample and its paired motor current sample for the resistance under load; IOBoard.md:475-476
gaps.description: Not found. FU-2D/003-P2-R9.json (found V187, read_at 2026-10-02T06:35Z): 'The tree does not state how fast motor current and cell voltage change between a cell sample and its INA228 current sample'. No P4 verifier re-read it. The ADBMS1818's 16 cell conversions against the INA228's conversion are therefore not aligned to any requirement. Listed in the owner's accepted open items (R9 found V187 not found in either round).

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V195 (R9, Cell monitor): whether the cell count comes from the balance lead or from SET_PACK_CELLS
gaps.description: Half found. FU-2D/003-P2-R9.json (found V195, read_at 2026-10-02T06:35Z): presence of a pack comes from the lead (battery_screen.h:19, :27); 'the cell count: not found'. No firmware or UI code reads SET_PACK_CELLS and nothing but the host tests fills battery_state_t.cells. FU-2C's answer 'from the setting' was refuted and the refutation stands (round2/FU-2C/018-adjudicator-R9.json). FU-2D/017-P4-datasheet-R9.json (read 2026-10-02T07:31:00Z) confirmed that the count is not found. Whether the ADBMS1818 can report the count of a 1 to 16 cell pack with no setting (V193) is therefore open.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V257, V259, V260 (R13, load-cell bridge ADC): rated capacity, smallest resolved load change and accuracy of each of the 3 load cells; IOBoard.md:499-500
gaps.description: Not found for the 2 torque cells. FU-C1/004-P2-R13.json (found V257, V259, V260, read_at 2026-09-29T02:40:15Z): thrust cell 980.7 N (100 kg TAS501) found; 'Torque cells: not read', because each torque cell's capacity is the torque range of V258 divided by the lever arm between the 2 cells, which is mechanical (round 3) and not stated in the tree. V259 (in N) and V260 (in % of rated output) for the torque cells depend on it, so only the thrust figures are found. R13 was not run in round 2. The ADS1235IRHBR and BD450M2FP3-CE2 were qualified against the thrust cell only.

gaps.spec_line: Research.md V11 (R1, USB protection): highest capacitance per line the protection may add on D+ and D-; IOBoard.md:148
gaps.description: The protection's share is not known. FU-2D/002-P2-R1.json (found V11, read_at 2026-10-02T06:25:12Z): USB 2.0 section 7.1.6.1 allows up to 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground per line at the transceiver and in the connector, with D+ and D- within 10 %; 'The RP2350 datasheet gives no capacitance for USB_DP and USB_DM (Table 1437), so the share left for the protection is not known'. FU-2D/009-P4-datasheet-R1.json confirmed that statement. The selected TPD6E05U06RVZR is held against a limit the research could not split.
